module: Double-ended queue (deque): items can be added and removed at the front as well as the back. Library by Pierre Chapuis (MIT license in the header). Useful for histories or sliding buffers. The object is a table indexed by integers between head+1 and tail.
usage:
local dq = require('dequeue').new()
dq:push_right(1); dq:push_right(2); dq:push_left(0)
print(dq:pop_left(), dq:length())  -- 0  2
notes: nil elements are forbidden by push (assert).
new(data) reuses the provided table as the queue (head/tail initialized to 0 if absent) and sets _serialize = true.
rotate_* on an empty queue returns nil; remove_left/right only remove the first occurrence found and shift the elements.
push_left/pop_left use indices <= 0: the table is no longer a pure Lua array (# is unreliable, use length()).

new.desc: Creates an empty deque, or turns the provided table into a deque.

data.desc: Existing table to reuse (may contain head/tail).

deque.desc: Object returned by new. Fields: head, tail, _serialize.

peek_right.desc: Returns the last element without removing it.

peek_left.desc: Returns the first element without removing it.

pop_right.desc: Removes and returns the last element.

pop_left.desc: Removes and returns the first element.

rotate_right.desc: Moves n elements from the end to the front.

rotate_left.desc: Moves n elements from the front to the end.

remove_right.desc: Removes the first occurrence of x, searching from the end.

returns.desc: true if an element was removed.

remove_left.desc: Removes the first occurrence of x, searching from the front.

returns.desc: true if an element was removed.

iter_right.desc: Iterator from the end to the front.

iter_left.desc: Iterator from the front to the end.

is_empty.desc: Tells whether the queue is empty.

contents.desc: Copies the content into an ordered array from 1 to length().

reset.desc: Resets head and tail to 0 (the old elements are not erased from the table).
